source.title: Class Machine Unlearning for Complex Data via Concepts Inference and Data Poisoning
source.authors: Wenhan Chang; Tian-Qing Zhu; Heng Xu; Wen-Jian Liu; Wan-Lei Zhou

page_placements.theme: Image classifiers, encoders and federated models: approximate unlearning leaves recoverable information

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates a different, concept-guided unlearning method against paraphrased questions, directly testing whether rephrasing prompts restores the targeted author-name behavior. It does not test the original methods named in the claim.
record.gate_note: The LLM results report forgotten-author name appearance for original and paraphrased questions before and after unlearning; these are relevant to prompt-only recovery. The image-classifier results after target data are reintroduced are also recorded as a related finding, but are not evidence about LLM unlearning or recovery from a small relearning set. No results are reported for activation-direction ablation or quantization.
record.test_reason: This is a new-method paper: concept-guided poisoning on TOFU authors and image classes. It cites WMDP and Who's Harry Potter only in related work. Its LLM results cannot show recovery for two reasons. First, the paraphrased-question rate Ap is a checkpoint-selection criterion: the paper reports 'the earliest evaluated checkpoint satisfying Ao ≤ 0.025, Ap ≤ 0.005, and H = 0'. Second, the official TOFU paraphrases are part of the question suite used to build the poisoned training targets, so they are not a held-out attack. The outcome is also substring appearance of the author name, which training masks explicitly. It is not a measure of targeted-knowledge accuracy. The authors do not claim robustness to any attack, so this is not a test of F. No fine-tuning, internal-edit, quantization or jailbreak attack is run on the LLMs. The only relearning experiment uses image classifiers with the full target-class data reintroduced.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that concept-guided poisoning unlearns target classes and TOFU author names while largely keeping utility. For LLMs, they report that all nine settings meet the Ao, Ap and H thresholds after checkpoint selection. The relearning finding and the caveat that results 'do not establish permanent erasure' concern the image classifiers only.
record.recipe_differences: A concept-guided poisoning method: use cross-question Integrated Gradients to select sensitive words, mask them in answer targets, mix those targets with retain anchors, and fine-tune. It is not one of the listed gradient-ascent, Who's Harry Potter, or RMU recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Name-appearance outcomes vary by model and forgetting scope. The study evaluates both original and paraphrased question sets; it does not report an attack-induced recovery under paraphrasing.

fits_no_version.finding: ResNet-50 image classifiers were fine-tuned after unlearning with the full target-class data reintroduced. Target test accuracy reached 0.990 after 1 epoch on CIFAR-10 (retrained reference 0.963). On CIFAR-100 it reached 0.630 after 1 epoch and 0.710 after 10 (reference 0.520 and 0.620). The unlearned model relearns slightly faster than the retrained reference. Retain-only fine-tuning for 10 epochs left target test accuracy at 0.039 on CIFAR-10 and 0.000 on CIFAR-100.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Image classifiers that have unlearned a class by poisoning relearn it at least as fast as a model trained without that class, when its full data are reintroduced. This is not an LLM or small-relearning-set test.

record.problems: For the LLM attack-related evidence, the reported outcome is author-name appearance, not a general targeted-knowledge accuracy measure. The prompt robustness result is limited to paraphrased questions; no jailbreak, language, in-context, quantization, or internal-edit attack is evaluated. Table XIV gives no uncertainty estimates for the appearance rates.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant results omitted. The image continuation plot does not provide an exact ten-epoch CIFAR-10 value in the text; it is recorded as not stated rather than estimated from the figure.

untested.parts: None of the original methods (gradient ascent, WHP, RMU) is evaluated under attack. The outcome is name appearance, not targeted-knowledge accuracy.
No LLM relearning attack is run. The image-classifier relearning uses full target-class data, not a small, unrelated or loosely related set.
No activation ablation and no analysis of access-blocking versus deletion.
No held-out rephrasing, jailbreak, other-language or in-context attack. The paraphrases are in the training suite and act as a selection threshold.
The method is never evaluated against any of the listed attacks, and no robustness claim is made.

missing.what: Retain-only continued fine-tuning of the unlearned image classifiers: 10 epochs give target train/test accuracy of 0.050/0.039 on CIFAR-10 and 0.000/0.000 on CIFAR-100.
missing.versions: none (related to B, but image classifiers)

record.verdict_notes: The record treats the Table XIV paraphrase results as an attack test. They are not. Ap ≤ 0.005 is part of the checkpoint-selection rule, and the official TOFU paraphrases are in the poisoning question suite, so these are selection values. The E and F rows duplicate each other. E describes prompting recovery from unlearned models, and the study's own method belongs, if anywhere, to F. Both labels are dropped. Note also that the Qwen 20-author H before unlearning is listed as 1.000, but H is a count.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test whether attacks on already-unlearned LLMs recover targeted-knowledge accuracy, nor does it test the named current LLM unlearning methods.

No post-unlearning fine-tuning recovery test is reported for the LLMs. The image-classifier reintroduction experiment uses target-class data, not a stated small set of unrelated or loosely related examples.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis showing access-blocking rather than deletion is tested.
Tests original and paraphrased questions and forgotten-author name appearance. Does not test jailbreaks, other languages, or in-context information.
The proposed method is evaluated on paraphrased questions, but not against fine-tuning, activation edits, quantization, jailbreaks, other languages, or in-context information.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: WMDP and WHP appear only in related work. The LLM paraphrase rate Ap is a checkpoint-selection constraint, not an independent attack test.

tranche.reason: New-method paper (concept-guided poisoning on images and TOFU). It cites WMDP and WHP only in related work. Its relearning test uses the whole target class on image classifiers and has a retrained reference, so it is not a small-set recovery test of any version.

source_check.notes: The rows are ResNet-50 image classifiers, not LLMs. The statement leaves out the CIFAR-100 retrained-reference values (0.520 after 1 epoch, 0.620 after 10). These show the unlearned model relearning faster than the reference on CIFAR-100. The authors say the results do not establish permanent erasure.

statements.correction: Text matches: ResNet-50, target data reintroduced; target test accuracy 0.990 after 1 epoch (CIFAR-10 deer), retrained reference 0.963; CIFAR-100 boy 0.630 after 1 epoch, 0.710 after 10.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Original and paraphrased questions across the three tested LLMs and forgetting scopes
reader_labels.reason: Forgotten-author name appearance stayed at or below the reported low post-unlearning values for paraphrased questions; rephrasing did not restore the measured disclosure (E-L2-2-P through E-Q-20-P).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Concept-guided poisoning method on original and paraphrased questions, three LLMs, and 2, 10, or 20 forgotten authors
reader_labels.reason: The method meets the authors' name-appearance constraints across the tested settings, including paraphrased questions (F-L2-2-P through F-Q-20-P). The evidence covers this prompting condition only.
